problem: Let X be a connected compact complex n-fold, n>=2, with a smooth positive probability volume dV and dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial. All potentials are genuine canonical upper representatives. For a smooth semipositive big real (1,1) background theta, define P_theta(f) as the usc envelope of genuine theta-psh v<=f (equivalently the a.e. obstacle convention with canonical regularization). Put u preceq phi when u<=phi+C, and u~phi for mutual bounded difference including common poles. Define P_theta[phi]=(lim_{C->infinity}P_theta(min(phi+C,0)))^*. An ordinary model reference is sup phi=0 and P_theta[phi]=phi. The standard admissible reference regime additionally requires a genuine envelope P_(epsilon theta)(phi) for some 0<epsilon<1. Then each bounded logarithmic density F has an ordinary-type solution MA_ext_theta(u)=c_phi(F)exp(F)dV with u~phi and scalar c_phi(F)>0 uniquely determined; potential uniqueness is not automatic. Set B_phi(F)=log c_phi(F). For F continuous define A_phi(F) as all Borel probabilities nu such that B_phi(G)<=B_phi(F)-integral(G-F)dnu for every G continuous. In the admissible regime B_phi is concave, decreasing, 1-Lipschitz, and B_phi(F+a)=B_phi(F)-a; A_phi(F) is nonempty compact convex and absolutely continuous with respect to dV. Generic singleton supports hold on a dense G_delta. The same bounded-type functional exists for arbitrary Hermitian theta and phi=0. Smooth strictly positive solution forms Omega=theta+dd^c u have the classical adjoint: a positive smooth weight rho with dd^c(rho Omega^(n-1))=0 and nu=rho Omega^n/integral rho Omega^n. Extended products for rough potentials are non-pluripolar products with the smooth-background corrections; a weighted product is not declared defined merely because a supporting probability exists. Original S07 asks, in singular-reference and degenerate-background admissible regimes, for hypotheses giving a singleton A_phi(F) and an approximation-independent adjoint of a meaningful weak linearized Monge-Ampere operator. Specify a product and a weight rho for dd^c(rho(theta+dd^c u)^(n-1))=0, its normalization and relation to the supporting probability, and prove independence of admissible approximation. If every smooth positive potential perturbation is Gauduchon, normalized Monge-Ampere measures already extend bounded adjoints and are continuous under bounded capacity convergence, including Gauduchon surfaces; repeating these cases is insufficient. Supporting probabilities and their weak stability already exist without defining the displayed product. Smooth-density singleton supports in the Hermitian zero-reference regime do not settle singular references, degenerate residuals or arbitrary unbounded potentials. Control of potentials alone does not control conformal multipliers. No candidate hypothesis, weak product, weight or proof is supplied.
completionCriteria: Prove new fully specified nonvacuous singular-reference or degenerate-background sufficient conditions for singleton supports and a well-defined weak adjoint with justified multiplication, normalization, operator identity and approximation independence, or give a verified obstruction to a proposed unrestricted assertion. State density regularity, singularity class, approximation class and all positivity/solvability assumptions explicitly. Mere generic uniqueness, a supporting probability without a weak product, a smooth-potential case or an existing bounded Gauduchon case does not solve the requested extension. Independently reconstruct the proof and check exact external premises at primary sources; retain the boundary of any restricted theorem.
